featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a new South Indian food spot in the city so I had to check it out. Nanna House in Bandra is serving Andhra style food and I tried their specials. The Karam Podi Dosa is your usual slick dosa, but with Karam Podi masala which was too spicy for me. The Pesarattu, a healthy moong dal dosa, was perfect though. I really enjoyed it. Another of their healthy offerings is the Millet Cone Idli, served in this very cute manner. It is plain and pasty, and a must try. All of this comes with 4 chutneys, each with their own kick. What you can’t miss here at all is their Filter Kaapi Soft Serve - it’s like creamy cold coffee. So good. Overall, this place offers unique and healthy options, so if that’s what you like, check it out.

featured_reviews.name: sucheta thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
If there’s one place Bandra needs to start forming lines for, it’s @nannahouseindia on 16th Road. This Andhra-style spot is all set to change the way Bandra — actually, Bombay — experiences South Indian food. And yes, maybe it sounds like I’m exaggerating… but one meal here is enough to prove why I’m not.

From the moment the food arrived, everything reminded me of the kind of flavours that feel simple, comforting, yet absolutely unforgettable.

We started with the Pesarattu, beautifully stuffed with upma — a combination that instantly transported me back to Hyderabad. The texture, the seasoning, the warmth… it just hits in the most nostalgic way.

Next up was the star of the show: the Butter Masala Dosa. Cooked in Amul butter and finished with a generous dollop of white butter, this dosa is easily one of the best in Bombay. Crisp edges, a soft centre, flavour-packed masala — truly dosa heaven.

The Butter Podi Idli followed the same theme — soft idlis coated in podi and topped with white butter. Comforting, buttery, and delicious in every bite.

And of course, no South Indian meal is complete without Filter Coffee. Their version is strong, aromatic, and balanced — exactly how a proper filter coffee should be.

But the surprise winner? The Filter Coffee Soft Serve. Smooth, perfectly sweet, full of coffee flavour — honestly, the perfect end to this meal. I’d go back just for this. ❤️

In a city overflowing with restaurants, Nanna House India stands out for its authenticity, warmth, and flavour-packed dishes. What are you waiting for? This is the place Bandra needs queues for — and trust me, once you try it, you’ll understand why.

1) Karam Podi Dosa – Felt dry and was served cold.
2) Ghee Podi Idli – Hardly any podi, and the idli was way too soft — almost like it wasn’t cooked properly.
3) Millet Cone Idli – Nice and different, but they can totally skip the ice-cream stick.
4) Filter Kaapi – Tasted good, but sugar should be on the table. We had to ask twice before we got it.
5) Chutney – Would be great if they could increase the quantity a bit.

With regard,
Team Nānna House

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are searching for authentic Andhra food in Bandra, Nanna House is a place you should not miss. This South Indian cafe specialises in traditional Andhra cuisine, and the flavours truly reflect home-style cooking. The millet cone idlis were soft and wholesome, and the podi idlis had the perfect balance of ghee and spice.

The dosa selection is excellent. The karam podi dosa was spicy, crisp, and full of flavour, while the butter masala dosa was comforting and indulgent. Every dish felt freshly prepared and true to South Indian food traditions, making it one of the better South Indian restaurants in Bandra.

The highlight for me was the putharekulu dessert, a rare Andhra sweet that is difficult to find in Mumbai. Light, ghee-rich, and delicately sweet, it ended the meal beautifully. Add a cup of traditional filter coffee and the experience feels complete. Highly recommended for anyone looking for the best Andhra restaurant in Bandra.

We visited Avatara for dinner to celebrate our 19th wedding anniversary, and it was an exceptional experience from start to finish. Their thoughtfully curated 16-course menu, inspired by the Indus Valley and complemented by traditional regional flavors from across India, was truly unique and memorable.
Every course—from the appetizers to the mains and desserts and also Paan ... was beautifully presented and expertly explained by Anirudh, whose warm hospitality added greatly to the evening. Every dish had a surprise twist to it.
We were also surprised with a lovely cake for our anniversary celebration, which made the occasion even more special.
Avatara offers a true gastronomic journey, and I would highly recommend it to anyone who appreciates innovative vegetarian cuisine. A must-visit for food lovers.

As a whole, the restaurant was comparable to Michelin Star restaurants we have visited around the world.

The atmosphere in the restaurant was lovely, with gentle music and a violinist playing live music throughout.

We ordered the 16 course menu with wine pairing. Food arrived promptly and the waiters explained each dish and the respective pairings well. The dishes were very thoughtful and creative, adding to the eating experience. Every dish hit the spot.

Overall it seemed really good value for the type of food, especially when compared to Europe, where we are from.

Would recommend visiting, and will be recommending it to everyone I know.

featured_reviews.name: Stanley Vaz
featured_reviews.review_text:
At Avatara, one does not merely dine—one participates in a carefully orchestrated culinary narrative that challenges every preconceived notion of vegetarian cuisine.

From the moment you are seated, the service establishes its quiet authority: attentive without intrusion, polished without pretension. Among the team, Viraj stands out—not with flamboyance, but with a rare, intuitive finesse. His understanding of the menu is not rehearsed, but lived; each course arrives not just as food, but as a story, delivered with precision and warmth.

The cuisine itself is nothing short of revelatory. In a world where vegetarian fare is often relegated to the periphery, Avatara asserts dominance. Every plate is a study in balance—texture, temperature, acidity, and depth all meticulously calibrated. Ingredients are elevated beyond their humble origins, transformed into expressions that are both rooted and avant-garde.

What distinguishes Avatara is its restraint. There is no unnecessary theatrics, no overindulgence in molecular excess. Instead, the kitchen demonstrates confidence—allowing flavours to speak, yet ensuring each bite leaves a lasting impression. It is this quiet mastery that aligns the restaurant with the philosophy of Michelin-starred establishments.

In its totality, Avatara delivers an experience that is immersive, thoughtful, and deeply satisfying. It is not simply one of the finest vegetarian meals—it is one of the finest meals, period.

**“Extremely disappointing and mentally frustrating experience. I ordered 2 Masala Dosa and 2 boxes of Medu Wada (each box containing 4 pieces, around ₹211 each), along with a watermelon juice add-on.

Shockingly, I did not receive the Medu Wada at all. I only received 2 boxes containing Masala Dosa with chutney and sambhar.

When I contacted the restaurant, they first told me to check properly and said there should be 3 boxes. After confirming with their kitchen, they firmly stated that everything was packed and sent correctly. Then they shifted the responsibility, saying if anything happens during transit, it is Zomato and the delivery partner’s issue.

But this is where the real problem lies. Instead of taking accountability or properly investigating, responsibility is being passed around. This creates a system where no one is answerable, and the only person who suffers is the customer who paid honestly.

Also, blaming the delivery stage so casually makes no sense. A delivery partner is not just a middle person—they are the backbone of this entire system. Without them, restaurants cannot deliver food and platforms cannot function. Indirectly shifting blame without clarity or resolution only reflects poor coordination and lack of accountability in the entire process.

In the end, both the restaurant and Zomato get paid, but the customer is left with incomplete food, no proper explanation, no immediate support, and only different excuses from everyone involved.

This is not just about a missing item, it reflects a deeper issue of responsibility, coordination, and customer respect. Very irresponsible service and a truly disappointing experience.”**

“If the system cannot ensure accountability, then the customer will always be the weakest and most ignored part of it.”

Overall, the restaurant scores high on food, service, and ambiance. Whether you're a vegetarian or just someone who loves good food, this place is sure to leave you impressed.

Paid premium price for a thoroughly mediocre experience, Eve was an absolute disappointment.

The staff seemed poorly trained and completely unprofessional, honestly felt like they had no hospitality background. The entire floor was chaotic, people shouting across sections, and managers constantly rearranging tables to squeeze in more guests. At one point, a table right next to us was given to new customers without even being cleaned.

Basic service etiquette was missing, plates weren’t changed unless we explicitly asked. On top of that, staff would hover right next to the table and the moment you finished a dish or drink, they’d immediately push you to order something else. It felt more like pressure than service.

Coming to the food, extremely underwhelming.
Nachos were the only decent dish. The mango salad had barely 7–8 pieces, the spaghetti was basic and poorly executed. Even classic cocktails like a Manhattan (served in the wrong glass!) and an Espresso Martini were messed up. Only the Picante managed to save some face.

Apart from the staircase with the “library” aesthetic, which is clearly designed for Instagram - there’s nothing special about this place.

For ~₹3,500 per person, this experience was nowhere close to worth it. There are far better restaurants in the city.

Avoid this place if you value your money and experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ A Complete Meal with the Perfect Sweet Ending!
This plate is a true celebration of flavors, from royal Awadhi kebabs to a classic dessert.
The Lucknow Gosht Galawati Kebab is the absolute star — incredibly soft, delicately spiced, and so tender that it melts in your mouth. Each bite reflects authentic Awadhi craftsmanship, rich yet perfectly balanced.
The Kafta (Kofta) Kebab is equally satisfying — juicy, flavorful, and cooked to perfection with a lovely outer crust and a moist, well-seasoned center. Paired with the light sautéed vegetables and the creamy baked cheesy side, the plate feels complete and thoughtfully curated.
To refresh the palate, the Big Cola (600 ml) does its job perfectly — chilled, fizzy, and refreshing.
And then comes the highlight of the ending — the Caramel Custard 🍮
Smooth, silky, and perfectly set, with just the right amount of caramel bitterness balancing the sweetness. It’s light, comforting, and an ideal way to close such a rich meal.
✔️ Authentic Awadhi taste
✔️ Excellent texture & balance
✔️ Well-presented, satisfying portions
✔️ Dessert that truly completes the experience
A meal that feels indulgent yet comforting from start to finish.
Highly recommended for kebab lovers and anyone who enjoys ending their meal on a sweet, classic note. 🌟🔥

featured_reviews.name: AP JP
featured_reviews.review_text: Lunch at the iconic K Bhagat Tarachand, an eatery that serves some wonderful thali since 1895 in Mumbai.  Their lunch service closes at 3.30 so I took an auto to reach the outlet closest to me in Andheri East, just outside the local train station and ordered myself a KBT Combo, a limited thali priced at 419 including taxes.  The thali had a paneer mixed curry, a mixed vegetable curry, a dal fry, with some jeera rice, with 2 pieces of their legendary desi ghee chapati, with a side of masala chaas / buttermilk, roasted papad and a farsan or starter of the day which was a dahi bhalla.  Initially for a limited quantity thali like this, I felt the price point to be very steep, but the quality of the food overlooked the quantity, needless to say the taste was exceptional.  The dahi bhalla, super soft, tender bhalla soaked and seasoned in sweet curd, is a fabulous start.  The paneer sabzi was nothing short of excellence in terms of spice and flavour and both the dal and the mixed veg sabzi had just the right heat to get through the desi ghee overloaded chapatis that were super soft and extremely wellmade.  The jeera rice was much needed to finish off the subzi and dal and the soft indulgent gulab jamoon was waiting to be savoured.  It was a delectable feast that I enjoyed thoroughly paired with some friendly service.  These people are specialists and the thali that I indulged in has taken 100+ years to perfect.  The masala chaas was a perfect accompaniment with the meal.  If you are looking for value you may not find this place suitable, but if you are looking for quality and exceptional taste, you will appreciate this thali that comes highly recommended.
